title: Pixel art editing is up on Retro Diffusion!
author: RealAstropulse
selftext:
Thought it would be a lot longer before this was possible, but it works and it looks awesome! So excited to see what people make with this.

For now it's just able to be used on generated images with the "RD Plus" model, but soon I'll be adding a section for editing \*any\* pixel art image you upload. That feature is already available [on the API](https://github.com/Retro-Diffusion/api-examples?tab=readme-ov-file#image-editing) for anyone who wants to use it for their own products.

Otherwise, head to [https://www.retrodiffusion.ai](https://www.retrodiffusion.ai) to start generating some pixel art!

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: Thanks! It was a lot of work to develop but I could not be happier with where its at and the new stuff still in the works.

comments.author: BerserkJeff88
comments.body: Does retro diffusion let you set a color palette to be used?

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: Yep! Down at the bottom of the settings on the left side

comments.author: 489Herobrine
comments.body:
Big fan of your tool Astro, I use it for downscaling images down to sprites for placeholders (Just setting no style 3% change image to image works great).

This is a banger new option, but could you implement image posing via either control net or even just image to image? It'd be very helpful to be able to adjust sprites into new dynamic poses for stuff like attack keyframes.  
  
My only gripe with the website so far was lacking that, I just wanna make attack placeholders in a fighting game lmao. Even better if you can incorporate it into the edit feature to maintain some level of character consistency between poses.

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: Trying! Unfortunately controlnet doesn't exist for the models we use and they dont take well to training for it. We're working on something like this for the image editor though.

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: Nudity/gore, yes. Sex acts, no. The models also are not capable of generating that content.

comments.author: ClassicGamer76
comments.body: Stills do not make a game. Animation of the characters is key. You probably have a longer way to go when taking the artist out of the whole pixel art process.

comments.author: firestell
comments.body: Hey I don't have this button, was this removed?

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: Yep! Maintains the pixel grid, and is actually styled for it. Not just downscaled.
